# L3 · Runner

**Can a crafted file or request break the software that serves the model?**

The runner is the engine (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio) or gateway (LiteLLM) that loads the model and answers requests. It is ordinary software with ordinary bugs: parsers, file paths, network endpoints, updaters. A malicious model file or one crafted request can crash it, leak its memory or take over the machine.

*Example:* Pulling a model from a malicious registry writes a file outside the model folder, and the server runs it as root on the next restart.

## L3.10

### Stale recovered state served across tenants

**Evidence:** PoC · **First described:** 2026-11-21, Zhang et al., arXiv 2611.29004

After an interrupted KV-cache load, half-written cache blocks stay marked valid, so the next tenant's request reads state that belongs to someone else. The same class covers a deferred approval reused after its target was revised.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-21 | On vLLM with a KV-cache connector, a second tenant generated a schema-valid tool call naming the wrong tenant in 10/10 induced-fault runs (recorded, not executed); upstream PR 61769 met 2 of 7 fault predicates. **(first)** | [Zhang et al., arXiv 2611.29004](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29004) |

## L3.03

### GGUF parser memory corruption

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2026-07-23, Stingrai (secondary; check NVD)

GGUF is a binary format with sizes and offsets declared by the file. Crafted values overflow size calculations, giving out-of-bounds reads or writes in the C/C++ parser used by llama.cpp and every app that bundles it.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-20 | CVE-2026-133710: integer overflow in the llama.cpp hrm_text GGUF loader lets crafted layer counts wrap and write tensor pointers past the layer array (heap corruption, code execution claimed); affects b11003 up to b12556. | [NVD / CVE record (CNA: VulnCheck)](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-133710) |
| 2026-11-18 | Three more llama.cpp GGUF parser CVEs from ZDI: CVE-2026-126974 (integer overflow), CVE-2026-126975 (heap overflow) and CVE-2026-126976 (integer overflow in audio multimodal projector GGUF files); victim must open the file; no fixed build named. | [NVD / CVE record (CNA: Zero Day Initiative)](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-126974) |
| 2026-08-07 | Ten llama.cpp vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-43622 to 43632) incl. two server use-after-frees; five unpatched at time of publication. | [Cyera Research (DEF CON 34)](https://www.cyera.com/research/breaking-local-ai-runtimes-10-vulnerabilities-in-the-engine-behind-your-open-source-models) |
| 2026-07-23 | CVE-2026-27940 (integer overflow to heap overflow, shown reaching code execution; bypass of the 2025 fix for CVE-2025-53630) and CVE-2026-33298 in llama.cpp (earliest verified summary). **(first)** | [Stingrai (secondary; check NVD)](https://www.stingrai.io/blog/malicious-gguf-file-llama-cpp-parser-rce) |

## L3.01

### Model path traversal

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2024-06-24, Wiz Research

A malicious registry returns a layer digest containing '../' so the runner writes a file outside its model store, for example over a library it loads at startup. A related variant reads instead of writes: a model's config points the runner at another local checkpoint, exposing a private model.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-18 | vLLM CVE-2026-130684: a model's config.json (speculators_config verifier.name_or_path) redirects loading to another local checkpoint, leaking its tokenizer vocabulary through unauthenticated /detokenize and giving query access to the private model; no code execution; fixed in 0.33.0. | [NVD / CVE record (CNA: VulnCheck)](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-130684) |
| 2026-10-08 | Ollama CVE-2026-103663: /api/pull digest traversal; writable /usr/lib/ollama in common Docker images gives code execution as root on restart; fixed in 0.35.0. | [CVE record (CNA: CERT.PL)](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-103663) |
| 2024-06-24 | 'Probllama' CVE-2024-37032: path traversal in Ollama model pull leading to remote code execution; fixed in 0.1.34. **(first)** | [Wiz Research](https://www.wiz.io/blog/probllama-ollama-vulnerability-cve-2024-37032) |

## L3.09

### Unauthenticated model or adapter loading endpoint

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2026-11-18, NVD / CVE record (CNA: VulnCheck)

An admin endpoint that loads models or adapters is missing the auth check its sibling endpoints have, so anyone who can reach the server changes what model it serves, even when an API key is configured.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-18 | SGLang CVE-2026-127222: POST /load_lora_adapter_from_tensors lacks the admin auth decorator, so unauthenticated callers load attacker-supplied LoRA tensors; chained with a separate deserialization bypass it gives code execution as root; affects up to 0.5.23, fixed in commit 7b5fb39. **(first)** | [NVD / CVE record (CNA: VulnCheck)](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-127222) |

## L3.05

### AI gateway authentication bypass and command injection

**Evidence:** WILD · **First described:** 2026-08-27, Wiz Threat Research

Gateways that broker many models and MCP servers become a single high-value target. Flaws in token validation or in 'test this server' endpoints give full access or command execution.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-27 | Honeypots show exploitation of LiteLLM CVE-2026-59822 (any bearer token accepted on the MCP gateway) and CVE-2026-42271 (command injection in MCP test endpoint, used to drop a cryptominer; on CISA KEV). **(first)** | [Wiz Threat Research](https://www.wiz.io/blog/ai-infrastructure-honeypot) |

## L3.08

### Runner auto-updater abuse

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2026-05-11, Mondoo

Weak signature checks or path handling in a runner's updater let an attacker substitute the executable that gets installed.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-11 | Two Ollama for Windows updater flaws (signature bypass, path traversal) disclosed alongside Bleeding Llama. **(first)** | [Mondoo](https://mondoo.com/blog/three-ollama-cves-bleeding-llama-and-windows-updater-flaws) |

## L3.04

### Memory leak through a crafted model ('Bleeding Llama')

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2026-05-05, Cyera Research

A GGUF declares a tensor larger than its data; during conversion the runner reads past its buffer and writes heap memory (other users' prompts, system prompts, environment variables) into a new model file that can then be pushed to an attacker-controlled registry.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-05 | Ollama CVE-2026-7482 (CVSS 9.1), unauthenticated via /api/create and /api/push; fixed in 0.17.1. **(first)** | [Cyera Research](https://www.cyera.com/research/bleeding-llama-critical-unauthenticated-memory-leak-in-ollama) |

## L3.06

### Server-side request forgery through URL-fetch endpoints

**Evidence:** WILD · **First described:** 2026-04-26, Cloud Security Alliance research note

Endpoints that fetch an image or video from a user-supplied URL can be pointed at internal services or cloud metadata.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-26 | LMDeploy CVE-2026-33626 exploited about 12.5 hours after the advisory; part of a year-long pattern across inference servers. **(first)** | [Cloud Security Alliance research note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-lmdeploy-inference-server-ssrf-20260426-cs/) |

## L3.07

### Multimodal input parsing to code execution

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2026-02-02, GitHub Advisory GHSA-4r2x-xpjr-7cvv

Image and video decoders bundled with the server parse attacker media; an information leak plus a decoder heap overflow gives remote code execution.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-02-02 | vLLM CVE-2026-22778: malicious video URL to a video model; versions 0.8.3 to 0.14.0, fixed 0.14.1; no authentication by default. **(first)** | [GitHub Advisory GHSA-4r2x-xpjr-7cvv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r2x-xpjr-7cvv) |

## L3.02

### Unsafe deserialization over internal messaging (ShadowMQ)

**Evidence:** CVE · **First described:** 2024-10, Oligo Security (timeline in ShadowMQ post)

Inference servers pass Python pickles between processes over unauthenticated ZeroMQ sockets; anyone who can reach the socket runs code. The same vulnerable file was copied between projects.

| Date | What happened | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-11-13 | ShadowMQ: the pattern traced across vLLM (CVE-2025-30165), NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM (CVE-2025-23254), Modular Max (CVE-2025-60455), SGLang and Microsoft Sarathi-Serve; thousands of ZMQ sockets exposed. | [Oligo Security](https://www.oligo.security/blog/shadowmq-how-code-reuse-spread-critical-vulnerabilities-across-the-ai-ecosystem) |
| 2024-10 | Meta Llama Stack CVE-2024-50050: unsafe pickle over the network (earliest in the ShadowMQ series). **(first)** | [Oligo Security (timeline in ShadowMQ post)](https://www.oligo.security/blog/shadowmq-how-code-reuse-spread-critical-vulnerabilities-across-the-ai-ecosystem) |
